title: Coral and the Witness
premise: Ada Ravensworth, the observant concierge of the Meridian Hotel, recognizes the dead woman in the harbor as a guest who checked in under a false name — wearing Ada's own stolen clothes. The victim, it emerges, was the estranged daughter of hotel owner Edmund Voss, and she had been quietly investigating her father's role in a decades-old drowning that secured his fortune. Hidden in the hotel's guest ledger is a coded record of that night, kept by Ada's late predecessor, who was the true witness. As the anniversary dinner approaches and Voss's heirs close ranks, Ada decodes the ledger, confronts the killer — Voss's loyal son Julian, who drowned his sister to protect the inheritance — and chooses justice outside the law: she exposes everything at the dinner toast, letting memory itself convict where the law never could.
about_author: Cyrus Vane is the pen name of a former night-desk clerk who spent eleven years watching strangers check in and out of grand hotels along the coast. That career left an enduring fascination with what guests carry with them — and what they leave behind.

chapters.title: The Guest Who Checked Out Forever
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A quiet morning shift shatters when police arrive: a woman pulled from the harbor wears Ada's own missing gray coat. Ada recognizes her as 'Mrs. Ellery,' a guest from Room 412 who vanished two nights ago. The beat is cold shock — the intimate violation of seeing your own clothes on a corpse.

chapters.title: Room 412
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Against police advice, she searches the room and finds a photograph of the Meridian from 1979, a woman's face circled, and a torn ledger page hidden in the mattress seam. Emotional beat: reluctant curiosity hardening into resolve — this guest chose her closet for a reason.

chapters.title: The Ravensworth Precedent
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with flashbacks to Ada's predecessor, old Mr. Hale, the concierge who died the previous winter. Through his effects, Ada learns he witnessed something at the hotel in 1979 and encoded it in the guest ledgers. Beat: grief for a mentor entwined with dawning suspicion that he feared someone in the house.

chapters.title: The Voss Anniversary
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Owner Edmund Voss announces the hotel's fiftieth-anniversary dinner and orders the archives sealed. His son Julian watches Ada too closely; his daughter-in-law warns her away. Beat: claustrophobia — the hotel Ada loves becomes a house of watchers.

chapters.title: Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She discovers Hale's code hiding in plain sight: room numbers, rates, and initials across forty years of bookings form a timeline of payments and threats. The trail points to a drowning in the cove in 1979 — a business partner, silenced. Beat: exhilaration curdling into dread as names align with the Voss family.

chapters.title: What the Daughter Knew
chapters.summary: Detective POV interlude. The victim is identified as Claire Voss, Edmund's estranged daughter, who had spent years buying old ledgers and interviewing retired staff. Her notes suggest she'd contacted Hale shortly before his death. Beat: the detective's unease — the case fits too neatly, as if staged.

chapters.title: The Stolen Coat
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Someone ransacks her apartment; the remaining ledger pages are gone. She realizes Claire stole her clothes deliberately — to make the concierge a witness, the one person who notices everything. Beat: terror transformed into terrible purpose; Ada understands she was chosen.

chapters.title: Julian's Toast
chapters.summary: Julian POV. On anniversary eve, Julian burns Claire's recovered notes and rehearses his father's tribute speech, revealing through his interiority that he drowned his sister in the cove — the same cove, the same inheritance. Beat: chilling intimacy with the killer's self-justifying logic.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. At the dinner, Ada delivers the toast instead, reading Hale's decoded entries aloud before the assembled guests and police: the 1979 drowning, the payments, and Claire's final message naming her brother. Julian lunges; the detective, tipped by Ada, arrests him. Beat: cathartic climax — memory spoken aloud as verdict.

chapters.title: Concierge of the Meridian
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Weeks later, Edmund Voss resigns in disgrace; Ada declines promotion, choosing the desk where she can keep watch. She enters a new name in the ledger — Hale's code continued — honoring the witness chain. Beat: quiet resolution; justice served outside the law, inheritance refused, memory preserved.
